about: Stage 2 of the story (src/Echo.cpp): the Echo Stones and the Reliquary. A freed city's altar raises an Echo Stone; walk up to it and it gives you that city's page, The Broken Words: <City> (a BOOK each), which says plainly which wonder-weapon part waits where and how to take it - and from then on your compass marks it. Parts: boss = dropped by that city's Barrow-Jarl; relic = a glowing reliquary at a landmark that only wakes at night, guarded (kill the guardians, then take it); kill = strike down the dead near a landmark at night until the barrow is fed. Each wonder needs its three parts, forged on its pedestal in the Reliquary behind the sealed door at High Hrothgar. Positions in Skyrim units (Tamriel or the HighHrothgar cell); yaw in degrees, clockwise from north.

wonders.label: Void Staff
wonders.text: A Falmer shaman's staff of black chitin and a violet eye that drinks the light: its orbs drag the dead together and crush them, and what it kills rises as spectral spiders that fight for you.

wonders.label: Rime Staff
wonders.text: A Falmer staff whose blue eye still holds the cold of Blackreach: its shards slow and freeze the dead, its blizzard locks a whole crowd in ice, and what is frozen shatters.

wonders.label: Storm Staff
wonders.text: A Falmer staff with a purple storm-eye: its lightning leaps between four of the dead, and its storm ball hangs in the air zapping everything near it.

wonders.label: Ember Staff
wonders.text: A Falmer staff with a red ember-eye that never cooled: its bolts burst into fire, and held it calls down a meteor that leaves the ground burning.

Riverwood.echo: The Betrayed came up out of the dark once, to the valley. Skjold took the violet eye from their shaman's staff, and the haft they left in the barrow on the mountain.
Riverwood.where: The Void Eye falls from Skjold Barrowborn himself - you took it when you freed Riverwood. The Void Staff's Haft waits at the doors of Bleak Falls Barrow, up the mountain path west of Riverwood.

Whiterun.echo: The shaman's mandibles were burned with the first dead of the plains at the cairn. The ash never cooled. It wants more of them.
Whiterun.where: Go to Dustman's Cairn, north-west of Whiterun across the plains. At night, cut down the dead around its door until the cairn has drunk enough; the Void Staff's Mandibles rise for you.

Solitude.echo: Potema took the storm-eye from a Falmer staff and set it in her circlet. The staff's mandibles she left with her wolves, in the cave where she was worshipped.
Solitude.where: The Storm Eye falls from the Wolf Queen's shade - you took it when you freed Solitude. The Storm Staff's Mandibles wait at the mouth of Wolfskull Cave, west of Solitude along the coast.

Windhelm.echo: Vrolund broke a Falmer staff of rime over his knee and buried the mandibles with his men in the barrow by the sea.
Windhelm.where: The Rime Staff's Mandibles wait at the doors of Yngol Barrow, north-east of Windhelm on the coast.

Markarth.echo: The Briar-Heart King pried the ember-eye from a Falmer staff found deep under the Reach, and wore it in his chest.
Markarth.where: The Ember Eye falls from the Briar-Heart King - you took it when you freed Markarth.

Riften.echo: The ember staff's haft was hung in the barrow above Ivarstead, where the Rift's old jarls still keep watch.
Riften.where: The Ember Staff's Haft waits at the doors of Shroud Hearth Barrow, above Ivarstead - far west of Riften, at the foot of the Throat of the World.

Falkreath.echo: Falkreath's Barrow-Jarl kept the ember staff's mandibles on a cord round his neck, and never put them down.
Falkreath.where: The Ember Staff's Mandibles fall from Falkreath's Barrow-Jarl - you took them when you freed Falkreath.

Morthal.echo: In the marsh, a storm staff's haft lies in the tomb under the Mire-Eye. It opens only when it has seen enough of the dead fall.
Morthal.where: Go to Ustengrav, north-east of Morthal in the marsh. At night, cut down the dead around its door until the tomb opens; the Storm Staff's Haft is yours.

Dawnstar.echo: The rime-eye froze in the temple on the hill, where the priests of dreams went mad. Only death thaws it.
Dawnstar.where: Go to Nightcaller Temple, on the hill east of Dawnstar. At night, cut down the dead around its door until the Rime Eye thaws; then it is yours.

Winterhold.echo: The rime staff's haft was taken north by Vrolund's enemies and sealed under the snow, where the sanctum keeps it.
Winterhold.where: The Rime Staff's Haft waits at the doors of Snow Veil Sanctum, south-east of Winterhold on the road toward Windhelm.

words.about: Stage 4 (src/Words.cpp): the Three Words. Once all four wonders are forged, Alduin's three words must be silenced one after another, each at its own place in the wilds and only at night: come near and the word's siege begins (waves of its dead round the place), and when the last wave falls the word's bearer rises. Kill it and the word is silenced for good - a power that stays with you, and the next word wakes. Saved in UN_EchoWords (bit per word; bit 8: the arc told). waves/elites per wave, health: x a zombie's night health (like the Barrow-Jarls).

rows.site: the Word Wall of Grah, in the Reach
rows.wake: GRAH. The first word shakes the ground under the Reach. A dragon priest who served Alduin in the Merethic Era answers it, and calls his barrow-dead to war around the wall that holds his word.
rows.silenced: The War-Priest falls and the word wall goes dark. GRAH is silenced: the battle-fury Alduin poured into the dead now runs in you.
rows.power: Battle-Fury: every weapon, bow, spell and wonder hits 15% harder.

rows.wake: DIR. The second word lies under Labyrinthian, the great tomb of Bromjunaar, where the dragon cult laid its dead by the thousand. Every one of them hears it.
rows.silenced: The Death-Thane crumbles in the courtyard of Bromjunaar. DIR is silenced: death has a weaker grip on you now.
rows.power: Death's Refusal: the night's blows hurt you 20% less.

rows.site: the summit of the Throat of the World
rows.wake: LEIN. The last word was shouted from the top of the world. Climb the Throat of the World at night: Alduin's echo still circles the summit, breathing his dead back into the world.
rows.silenced: The Echo of Alduin breaks apart over the summit and its shout dies on the wind. GRAH, DIR, LEIN - all three words are silenced. The World-Eater's curse is broken.
rows.power: The World Answers: your magicka returns half again as fast.
